title: Calibro: Compilation-Assisted Linking-Time Binary Code Outlining for Code Size Reduction in Android Applications
problem: Pre-compiled Android OAT files exhibit up to 25% code redundancy; reducing binary size is critical for constrained mobile storage and memory. Traditional link-time optimization misses redundancy.
motivation: Mobile devices have limited storage and memory; Android's pre-compilation creates large OAT binaries. Redundancy elimination directly reduces app footprint and improves launch performance.
method: Calibro reduces binary size by extracting duplicate code into single locations, using a two-stage process. During compilation, it identifies code regions that likely repeat. During linking (when all code is assembled into the final binary), it uses a parallel suffix tree—a fast data structure for detecting repeated patterns—to find actual duplicates and extract them. To avoid slowing the app, it only extracts code from infrequently-called functions.
key_novelty: It finds and removes duplicate code using compilation-stage hints to guide a fast link-time search, optimizing only infrequently-called functions to preserve performance.
contributions: Compilation-time + linking-time binary code outlining approach
Parallel suffix tree method for fast redundancy detection
Hot function filtering to prevent performance degradation
15.19% average code size reduction with negligible runtime overhead

metrics.other: 15.19% code size reduction, negligible runtime overhead

baselines: AOSP baseline with all optimizations enabled
limitations: Specific to Android OAT pre-compilation pipeline; applicability to other mobile platforms not discussed.
primary_theme: binary code outlining for Android app size reduction
